correctness.rationale: For odd primes \(p<q\), the published squarefree formula gives \(\Phi(pq)=(p-\beta(p))(q-\beta(q))\). The only possible cross-divisibility is \(p\mid q-\beta(q)\), yielding exactly two reduced classes modulo \(4p\). Fixed-modulus prime number theory gives the finite-prime main term; Brun--Titchmarsh bounds the middle prime range by a convergent tail of \(\sum 1/(p(p-1))\); and the large-prime range is \(O(X^{2/3})\). The packaged exact computation checks the local criterion through \(2,000,000\) and certifies the numerical constant interval.

value.rationale: The semiprime layer is the first composite layer on which G-cyclicity has genuine cross-prime obstructions. The result gives both the exact obstruction and its complete global mass, proving that exceptions have order \(X/\log X\) while the ambient odd squarefree semiprimes have order \(X\log\log X/\log X\). This supplies a natural structural and asymptotic invariant rather than merely extending a finite table.
